newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool to grow altered canola-SWP.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool to grow altered canola-SWP.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handler, Saskatchewan Wheat Pool on Tuesday said it entered into an agreement to develop and grow genetically altered canola oil products for Calgene Inc.

"By working with Calgene, we will ensure that our farmers and the agricultural industry share in the benefits offered by this powerful technology," SWP manager of research and development Bob Morgan said in a statement.
SWP expects to produce 500,000 acres of specialty canola under the agreement, the statement said.
Calgene officials were not immediately available for comment.

The agreement with SWP follows Calgene's oilseed licensing agreement with Monsanto Co granting Calgene a royalty free license to current and future agronomic technology developed by Monsanto, the SWP statement said.
Calgene will use the technology to develop new specialty canola oil products from the modified genes of its proprietary oils.
Canola oil is used in margarine and cooking oil and has the lowest saturated fat content of any oilseed at seven percent.
